newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura to take preventive steps, pay cuts.
newsitem.headline: Nomura to take preventive steps, pay cuts.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd is expected to unveil measures to prevent a recurrence of its latest scandal at the urging of the Finance Ministry, company sources said.
The steps are likely to include the establishment of a compliance committee comprising senior management, they said.
The sources also said that Nomura's senior executives will take salary cuts to take responsibility for the incident.
"Senior executives, not only the former president, are all responsible for the scandal," said one company source.
Nomura said on March 6 that two of its directors made apparently illegal deals involving a corporate client linked by media to racketeers.

A senior Finance Ministry (MOF) official told Reuters recently that the MOF urged Nomura to work out measures to avoid a relapse of such practices, adding that such measures should be taken regardless of the conclusion of an investigation by the nation's securities watchdog.
A Nomura spokesman said that a regular board of directors' meeting will be held on Wednesday, but said the topics of discussion have not yet been decided.
Last Friday, the Nomura Securities President Hideo Sakamaki resigned over the scandal and chairman Masashi Suzuki announced that he would serve additionally as president.
He said that his top priority was to restore trust in the company.
